title: Watchful Mama Bear Gemini Wins the Helicopter Mom Award
summary:
Even bears can be helicopter parents. The term describes parents who watch, control, and hover over their children all the time out of fear.

For being so watchful, the U.S. Forest Service team at Tongass National Forest in Alaska has given a brown bear named Gemini the 2026 Helicopter Mom Award.

"We understand her choice, weighing the dangers of being around other bears at a prime fishing location," the rangers write. "Still, we hope we see a lot more of them next year."

Gemini kept an eye on her cubs around other bears fishing in Alaska's Anan Creek. Brown bear cubs in Alaska have about a 50 percent chance of surviving their first year. Gemini has also had cubs in 2023 and 2024.
why_it_matters: Watching over young animals helps them stay safe, just like grown-ups watching over you near busy places.
